setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (4 reviews): Reviewer calls this Dark Star possibly the band's finest ever; Reviewer hears a classic version with jazzy jams and sweet noodling [4][6][7][8]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Show opens with Morning Dew, which the reviewer takes as a sign of a strong night [5]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Played fast, before the band slowed the song down in the mid-1970s [8]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Reviewer rates this Bird Song the best ever apart from Veneta and possibly 6/22/73 [9]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Reviewer says Jerry botched the solo; vocals elsewhere in the show are also sloppy [8]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Opens set two with sweet harmonies and a good jam that follows [6]

## The recordings

- **gd72-09-27.sbd.vernon.18106.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 171 min; rated 4.48/5 by 21 [1]
- **gd1972-09-27.170606.aud.nfagdtrfb.flac1648**: audience recording; 20 songs; 167 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Attendee was a high school senior who begged parents to go, as one night of the three-night run fell on a school night [7]
- Attendee and friends drank tequila outside; Morning Dew's first chord sounded as they walked into the theatre [12]
- A banner hanging from the balcony wished Pigpen a speedy recovery [12]
- Reviewer says the show reflects the intensity the band brought to the New York area since the 1968 Fillmore East show [4]
- Reviewer ranks the show among their five best from 1972, based on the Dick's Picks 11 release [6]
- Attendee considers this probably the strongest of the three Stanley shows [7]
- Reviewer counts it among favorite September 1972 shows, alongside 9/21, also a Dick's Pick [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-09-27.sbd.vernon.18106.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The show was released as Dick's Picks 11; reviewer also recommends the following night at the Stanley; The show is Dick's Picks 11, so the archive files were removed because it is sold officially [5][11]
- **gd1972-09-27.170606.aud.nfagdtrfb.flac1648**: taped by Unknown; source: Source-A: Unknown AUD > ? > TDK-AD (normal bias) cassette, via the Doug Lamarre collection. Source-B: Unknown AUD > ? > 7-inch reel @3.75ips, rescued from Ebay. [2]. Also: Audience-source file set; notes say this date is featured on Dick's Picks 11 [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by johnsdeadart.blogspot.com: [John's Custom Grateful Dead Album Cover Art](https://johnsdeadart.blogspot.com/2017/05/blog-post_90.html) [16]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Stanley Theatre - September 27, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/september-27-1972) [18]
